sections.heading: About Kiminou Knox
sections.text: Kiminou Knox is a Bay Area raised, New Orleans based author and poet with ten published books. He writes across poetry, faith, identity, love, family, imagination, and youth storytelling, hosts the KimYaps podcast, created the Black Boy Lie universe, and serves as a director at Artists and Athletes for Change.

sections.heading: Works
sections.text: The Spirit of Solomon; Our Father?; Hopeless Romantic; Poems From a Black Boy; Boys Raised in Silence; Why Did You Ghost Me?; My Father; 7.16.74: An Ode to Rashida; The Adventures of Kiminou the Great and Chua the Wise; Kiminou's World of Imagination: The Basics The official bibliography contains ten distinct published books: eight poetry collections and two children's books. My Father is published as a Remastered Edition, its only public edition. Other remastered formats are cataloged as editions of their originals, not counted as additional titles, and Black Boy Poems is the paperback title of Poems From A Black Boy.

sections.heading: "Protecting My Peace" Is Making You Lonely
sections.text: 2026-09-25. It's another late night, and I'm not going to lie to you. I am tired of hearing "I'm just protecting my peace." Are you protecting your peace? Or are you avoiding the real issues you don't want to face? In this episode, Kiminou Knox breaks down the difference between guarding your peace and dodging accountability. Protecting your peace is not always about removing people. Sometimes it is about doing the inner work...

sections.heading: You're Useful to Everyone Except Yourself
sections.text: 2026-09-24. In this late-night episode of KimYaps, host Kiminou Knox breaks down the Utility Trap — why so many of us confuse being needed with being loved. If you stopped fixing everybody's problems tomorrow, would they still call? Kiminou Knox gets honest about building your whole identity around being useful: the human flatbed truck everybody dials when they need hauling, but nobody checks on. He tells the story of his Ken...

sections.heading: Do You Like Me, or Do You Like Being Liked?
sections.text: 2026-09-20. The conversation delves into the complexities of modern dating, exploring the ambiguity and evasiveness prevalent in relationships. It highlights the challenges of navigating undefined connections and the emotional toll it takes on individuals. sections.text: 2026-09-20. The conversation delves into the complexities of modern dating and relationships, exploring themes of maturity, patience, and reciprocity. It challenges the romanticization of emotional unavailability and yearning, emphasizing the importance of engagement and reciprocation in relationships. The slowburn dilemma is dissected, highlighting the need for genuine movement and reciprocity in romantic connections. Takeaw...

sections.text: 2026-09-10. GO WHERE YOU’RE APPRECIATED, NOT WHERE YOU’RE TOLERATED | KIMYAPS What does it actually mean to be appreciated in a relationship? In this episode of KimYaps, Kiminou takes a phrase that sounds simple on Instagram and pulls it apart in real life: the difference between being loved, being needed, being tolerated, and actually feeling like your presence matters. From perceived partner responsiveness and rejection sen...

sections.heading: ANOTHER TUESDAY: TURNING 20, NASTY 19, AND THE MYTH OF GROWING UP
sections.text: 2026-09-10. ANOTHER TUESDAY: TURNING 20, NASTY 19, AND THE MYTH OF GROWING UP I turn 20 in 23 days. Ew. There’s something about losing the “teen” at the end of your age that makes adulthood suddenly sound way more official than it actually feels. Nineteen still gives you an alibi. You make a terrible decision? You’re 19. Fall in love after three conversations at 2 in the morning? Nineteen. Spend money you absolutely should’ve...

sections.heading: God Knows Your Heart. Are You Sure That’s Good News?
sections.text: 2026-09-03. Everybody loves saying, “God knows my heart.” Okay. But have you ever actually thought about what that means? In this episode of KimYaps, Kiminou sits with the first five verses of Proverbs 21 and somehow ends up everywhere from basketball coaches and controlling parents to gossiping aunties, pride, procrastination, worship, and the little stories we tell ourselves so we can keep believing we were right. Because y...

sections.heading: Does God Actually Hate Gay People?
sections.text: 2026-09-03. What does Christianity actually mean when it calls homosexuality a sin, and why has the church done such a terrible job explaining it? In this episode of KimYaps, Kiminou talks through homosexuality, sexual acts, attraction, identity, the circle of life, sin, death, friction, church hypocrisy, Catholicism, the Black Church, and the difference between disagreeing with somebody and believing you have the right to co...

sections.heading: The Abandoned Son and the Caged Daughter: How Childhood Wounds Shape Love
sections.text: 2026-06-25. The conversation delves into the meeting of two survivors of childhood trauma and the impact of family dynamics on their psychological development. It explores the daughter's upbringing, the son's experience, their initial meeting, the unconscious dance of projection and defense, inner work and healing, conscious naming and neural integration, and the process of building a new sanctuary. Takeaways Survivors of chi...

sections.heading: Adam, Eve, and Black Love
sections.text: 2026-06-25. The conversation delves into the psychological exploration of love, archetypes, and the impact of systemic trauma on African American relationships. It highlights the suppression of vulnerability, the projection of toxic media narratives, and the importance of reclaiming projections and inner gold. The journey of reconciliation, shared vulnerability, and the symbolism of the Mandorla in relationships are emphasize...

sections.heading: Psychology Of The Abandoned Son
sections.text: 2026-06-24. The episode explores the psychological impact of father absence on sons, delving into the themes of abandonment, silence, overachievement, rebellion, mother-son dynamics, the search for masculine guidance, impact on intimate relationships, the shadow side of abandonment, literary archetypes, the necessity of forgiveness, reparenting and inner healing, breaking the generational curse, and transformation and resilie...

sections.heading: Black Mothers, Black Daughters, and What We Inherit
sections.text: 2026-06-24. The toxic mother-daughter dynamic in black households is a complex and multi-layered issue, shaped by history, trauma, and the struggle for survival. It involves the interplay of strength, control, and the internalization of external sieges. Liberation from this dynamic is a revolutionary act of reclaiming one's humanity and breaking free from the cage of inherited pain. Takeaways Toxic mother-daughter dynamics in...

sections.text: 2026-05-24. In this episode of KimYaps, Kiminou Knox talks through trauma bonds, Proverbs 21, love, healing, and what it means to let Christ correct the way we understand safety, attachment, and freedom. KimYaps is hosted by Kiminou Knox, a Bay Area raised, New Orleans based author and poet of ten published books, speaker, and youth-centered builder. routes.description: Essays and poems by Kiminou Knox on faith, identity, love, discipline, writing, basketball, and Black boy life.

sections.heading: Author's Journal
sections.text: The Lie I Was Told About Discipline: Discipline is not about wanting to. Discipline is about doing it anyway when the return is not visible yet. On Love That Does Not Perform: I keep writing about love because I keep trying to understand it as practice, not performance. Ten Books Before Twenty: Why I Could Not Stop: I reached ten published books before twenty. The real answer is that I could not stop. What I Mean When I Write About Faith: Faith in my work is not decoration. It is the wound I keep returning to because it has not resolved. The Court and the Page Are the Same Discipline: People ask how I balance basketball and writing. I do not. They have never been separate. What Black Boys Are Not Allowed to Feel: There is a performance tax placed on Black boys before they ever learn to speak. This is me refusing to keep paying it.

routes.description: Discipline is not about wanting to. Discipline is about doing it anyway when the return is not visible yet.

sections.heading: The Lie I Was Told About Discipline
sections.text: Discipline is not about wanting to. Discipline is about doing it anyway when the return is not visible yet.

sections.heading: Essay
sections.text: Discipline is not about wanting to. That is the lie. Motivation is unreliable. It comes and goes with sleep and season and whether the last thing you did worked or not. Discipline is what you do in the absence of motivation. The decision is made once. You show up because you decided to show up, and the showing up is its own justification.

routes.title: On Love That Does Not Perform - Kiminou Knox
routes.description: I keep writing about love because I keep trying to understand it as practice, not performance.
keywords: On Love That Does Not Perform

sections.heading: On Love That Does Not Perform
sections.text: I keep writing about love because I keep trying to understand it as practice, not performance.

sections.heading: Essay
sections.text: I keep writing about love because I keep trying to understand it. Not romantic love specifically, though that is in there. Love as a practice. Love as a discipline. Love without an audience. Love that does not know it is being watched. Genuine love is expensive. It costs presence, honesty, and time in a way that cannot be scheduled. That is the love I am interested in: not the feeling, but the practice.

keywords: Ten Books Before Twenty: Why I Could Not Stop

sections.heading: Ten Books Before Twenty: Why I Could Not Stop
sections.text: I reached ten published books before twenty. The real answer is that I could not stop.

sections.heading: Essay
sections.text: I reached ten published books before twenty. People ask how. The real answer is that I could not stop. Not as discipline, though that is part of it, but as necessity. The writing was the only place where the interior life had room to be what it actually was. Each book came from a specific season and a specific question I was living inside. Ten books means ten rooms I went through. It is not a ceiling. It is the record of where the work has taken me so far.

routes.title: What I Mean When I Write About Faith - Kiminou Knox
routes.description: Faith in my work is not decoration. It is the wound I keep returning to because it has not resolved.
keywords: What I Mean When I Write About Faith

sections.heading: What I Mean When I Write About Faith
sections.text: Faith in my work is not decoration. It is the wound I keep returning to because it has not resolved.

sections.heading: Essay
sections.text: I did not title a book Our Father? with a question mark to be provocative. I did it because the question was real. Faith in my work is not decoration. It is the wound. It is the thing I keep returning to because it has not resolved, because it keeps demanding something of me that I do not always have to give. Where I have landed, at least for now: faith is not a feeling. It is a discipline. It is the daily choice to orient yourself toward something you cannot see but believe has coherence.

routes.description: People ask how I balance basketball and writing. I do not. They have never been separate.
keywords: The Court and the Page Are the Same Discipline

sections.heading: The Court and the Page Are the Same Discipline
sections.text: People ask how I balance basketball and writing. I do not. They have never been separate.

sections.heading: Essay
sections.text: People ask how I balance basketball and writing. I do not. They have never been separate. The same thing that makes you show up to film study when you would rather not makes you sit down with a blank page when nothing is there yet. The discipline is not different. The failure looks different. The patience required is the same. Basketball taught me to show up when I am empty. Writing required the exact same thing. The practice continues whether the day feels good or not.

routes.title: What Black Boys Are Not Allowed to Feel - Kiminou Knox
routes.description: There is a performance tax placed on Black boys before they ever learn to speak. This is me refusing to keep paying it.
keywords: What Black Boys Are Not Allowed to Feel

sections.heading: What Black Boys Are Not Allowed to Feel
sections.text: There is a performance tax placed on Black boys before they ever learn to speak. This is me refusing to keep paying it.

sections.heading: Essay
sections.text: There is a performance tax placed on Black boys before they ever learn to speak. Before we know what grief is, we know what grief looks like when it is suppressed. I started writing at thirteen because the feeling would not fit anywhere else. It went onto the page, because the page asked nothing of me except honesty. My books are written in the language I was not supposed to learn. They are not performances of strength. They are accounts of what strength actually requires. Your feelings are not weakness. Your grief is real, and it is allowed to be put somewhere it will not destroy you.
